what: An oscillator made of short sine grains, for vocal, plucky or smeared tones.
how: Each cycle of the pitch contains a short burst (grain) of a sine at the formant frequency. FORMANT sets that grain's pitch and so the colour; SHAPE and BLEED change how the grains look and how much leaks between them, from clean to smeared.

ins.pitch: Pitch in octaves (1 volt per octave, 0 is middle C). Patch KEYS' pitch here.
ins.formant: A control signal that moves the formant. Each 1.0 of signal doubles its frequency (an octave).

knobs.formant: The grain frequency, 100 to 5000 Hz. Low is dark and round; high is bright and nasal.
knobs.shape: Waveshaping of the grain, 0 to 1. It changes how sharp or smooth the tone is.
knobs.bleed: How much formant leaks through between grains, 0 to 1. Fills in the gaps for a thicker, smeared sound.
knobs.tune: Shifts the pitch in semitones, -24 to 24 (two octaves down to two up), added to the pitch input.

try: Patch KEYS' pitch into GRAINLET's pitch, GRAINLET's out through a VCA and an AD into OUT. Play a low note while you sweep FORMANT up for a talking effect.
